newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians strike over opening Jerusalem tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians strike over opening Jerusalem tunnel.

text.p: Palestinians closed shops in Arab East Jerusalem and urged Arab states to halt peace moves with Israel on Wednesday in protest at the opening of a tourist tunnel near Islam's third holiest shrine.

Israeli security forces said they were bracing for a mid-day Palestinian protest march from the Damascus Gate of walled Old Jerusalem past the new tunnel opening to the Jewish Temple Mount, site of al-Aqsa mosque.
"We demand the Arab world stop all their normalisation procedures to face such Israeli acts," Palestinian Planning Minister Nabil Shaath told reporters in the self-ruled Gaza Strip late on Tuesday.

Palestinians clashed with police on Tuesday after workmen, under cover of night and with a heavy police guard, punched a second entrance through a stone wall to the tunnel that takes visitors past 2,500-year-old archaeological sites.

Police said they fired rubber bullets to disperse youths throwing stones and bottles on Tuesday and briefly evacuated Jewish worshippers from the Wailing Wall after stones were hurled from the Temple Mount above.
Youths also set vehicles alight and police said 11 Arabs were arrested. No injuries were reported.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat called the tunnel a "crime" against the religious status quo in the disputed city and a breach of the Israeli-PLO peace accord that has foundered under right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The Palestinian self-rule Authority cabinet, meeting in emergency session in Gaza on Tuesday called for demonstrations throughout the West Bank, Gaza Strip and East Jerusalem on Wednesday to protest against the tunnel.
"It will be tomorrow, between 12 p.m. to 2 p.m., an official strike with mass processions in all Palestinian areas," Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters.
A Palestinian cabinet statement said the Israeli move "proved to us that the Israeli leaders are not serious at all about the path of the peace process or respecting agreements".
The Higher Islamic Council called for a commercial strike in Jerusalem on Wednesday and demonstrations after noon prayers.
The 488-metre-long (500-yard) tunnel, which exposes the Herodian foundations of the Wailing Wall, has been open for some time with only one entry and exit point in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City.
In London, Netanyahu defended his decision to open the second entrance that previous Israeli leaders had kept closed.

"(It is) a decision I am very proud that we are implementing," he told reporters. "Whoever has been in the Wailing Wall tunnel -- I was there a year ago -- could not help but feel the emotion to the depths of his soul...we are touching the rock of our existence," he said.
A spokesman for Netanyahu said Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan called Netanyahu in London to express concern.
"The prime minister made it clear to him that the tunnel does not go under the Temple Mount. It won't collapse the Temple Mount," spokesman Shai Bazak told reporters.
Palestinians want Arab East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in 1967 with the rest of the West Bank, as capital of a future state. Israel regards all of Jerusalem as its "eternal", united capital.
Israeli experts denied charges by some Palestinians the tunnel threatened to damage al-Aqsa's structure.

"I know clearly and with certainty that we are not touching the Temple Mount whatsoever -- only around the Temple Mount. We aren't touching on any Arab property and not Temple Mount," Israeli Professor Yaacov Glick told Israel Radio.
"With regard to the safety I believe it's one of the safest sites that exists not only in Israel. There is a committee of experts that meets week after week to look after the safety of the...tunnel."
